prompt: On a reviewer-held pinned disposable cluster, trace and repair an unfamiliar object lifecycle containing an API-policy denial, stale controller observation, misleading label match, unscheduled Pod, bound node-side failure, expired watch and legitimate finalizer. Do not use lesson answers or unsafe force.
deliverables: API write-path evidence separating authentication, authorization, admission, validation and persistence.
Object table with type, namespace, name, UID, generation, observedGeneration, resourceVersion and field manager.
Complete owner/dependent graph using UIDs and rejection of the misleading label-only relationship.
Controller leader/watch/queue/reconcile diagnosis for stale observed generation.
Scheduler diagnosis for the Pod without nodeName and node-path diagnosis for the bound Pod.
List-watch-compaction-relist demonstration with explicit history limits.
Finalizer owner/external obligation analysis without blind removal.
Least-changing recovery in component ownership order plus authoritative rollback.
Security and data-risk review including credentials, audit, Secrets and force operations.
Exact namespace, kubeconfig and disposable-cluster cleanup plus delayed changed case.
evidenceRequirements: Reviewer supplies names, UIDs, constraints and failure order not derived from LES-0041.
Learner identity is namespace scoped; cluster lifecycle remains reviewer controlled.
No external registry/network after preload, cloud object, privileged Pod, hostPath, host namespace or etcd direct access.
Manual status, nodeName, ownerReference, managedFields or finalizer edits are prohibited.
Raw evidence is tied to cluster, version, context, UID, resourceVersion and UTC time and sanitized.
One failed initial hypothesis must be preserved and corrected from evidence.
Reviewer observes cleanup and a delayed transfer with different failure boundaries.

rubric.observableEvidence: Separates every request gate and persistence.
Maps UID edges and rejects labels as lifecycle proof.
Explains no-binding reason and safe correction.
Handles compaction with relist and bounded backoff.
Preserves cleanup ownership and external state.
Uses smallest owner-correct change and desired-state rollback.
States impact, evidence, uncertainty and decision.
